title: How to highlight the structure
coreMove: Make rank, sequence, and dependence visible on the page without pretending formatting can create logic.
sourcePressure: Chapter 6 turns to visible presentation: underlined points, decimal numbering, and indented display as ways to expose hierarchy so the reader need not reconstruct it.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Believing that numbering, underlining, or indentation will fix a structure that is still vague or mixed.

sourceAnchors.name: underlined points
sourceAnchors.detail: the Chapter 6 sidecar lists Underlined points as one authorized heading for making structure visible
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: An underlined point should tell the eye which claim governs the detail, not make every sentence shout equally.

sourceAnchors.name: decimal numbering and indented display
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar ties structure visibility to decimal numbering and indented display
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Numbering and indentation are useful only when their levels match the hierarchy the logic has already earned.

hook: A clean list hides mixed logic until someone asks why the items belong together
opening with an abstract definition of clarity
starting with a generic frustrated professional staring at a blank document
counterintuition: It is not about being concise; it is about being structured
clarity is not about writing less; it is about thinking better
structure sounds rigid but actually creates freedom
tryThisNow: Set a timer and rewrite the first paragraph
ask yourself what the point is
examples: teacher explains the same lesson with better wording
same protagonist revises a deck under meeting pressure
same scene as prior chapter with swapped document type

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective recognition, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm through a direct second-person passage, a short research/source aside, a reader question, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a medical-device quality manager preparing corrective-action evidence
exampleSpecs.audience: regulated quality teams writing inspection responses
exampleSpecs.stakes: inspectors may miss which evidence supports which corrective action if the page treats every line equally
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anna underlines only the governing corrective actions, indents each evidence item beneath its parent, and removes emphasis from details that had been competing with claims.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A blue inspection stamp dries beside a stack of corrective-action forms.

exampleSpecs.domain: a film festival scheduler explaining screening conflicts
exampleSpecs.audience: event teams coordinating rooms, rights, and guest travel
exampleSpecs.stakes: volunteers will misroute guests if the schedule note hides dependency levels
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Diego replaces a flat list with decimal levels that show venue constraints, rights windows, and dependent guest-travel actions.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Two lanyards and a marked screening grid lie on the box-office counter.

exampleSpecs.domain: a fisheries regulator writing quota guidance
exampleSpecs.audience: policy staff who must show rule hierarchy
exampleSpecs.stakes: harvesters may follow exceptions as if they were main rules if the display is flat
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mikkel shows the old flat bulletin beside a revised indented version where exceptions sit visibly under the quota rule they modify.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Mikkel one angry harbor call to notice the exception looked like a rule.
mustAvoid: wildlife refuge invasive plants from ch5

exampleSpecs.domain: a bank fraud team documenting escalation rules
exampleSpecs.audience: risk teams writing procedures with nested decisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: frontline staff will escalate every alert if thresholds and subconditions are not visibly ranked
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "This looks like six equal rules," Catarina says, then indents subconditions under the two real escalation thresholds.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "This looks like six equal rules," Catarina says beside the fraud queue.

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth soccer league publishing playoff tiebreaker rules
exampleSpecs.audience: volunteer administrators writing rules parents will scan fast
exampleSpecs.stakes: a disputed playoff spot will be decided from the posted rule sheet
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam asks which rule should be read first, then uses numbering to reveal the tiebreaker sequence and indentation for subconditions.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which line will a parent read first when two teams are tied?

exampleSpecs.domain: a library acquisitions lead explaining collection cuts
exampleSpecs.audience: public-sector readers scanning a difficult policy note
exampleSpecs.stakes: branches will assume the wrong materials are protected if the governing criteria are not visibly distinct
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Kasia underline only the three selection criteria and indent examples so the branch managers can see they are examples, not new rules.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are standing beside a cart of withdrawn books and a draft policy sheet.

skillTargets: use formatting to reveal hierarchy rather than decorate text
select underlining, numbering, or indentation for the right structural need
spot when display hides weak logic
preserve deductive or inductive movement visibly on the page

tryThisNowSpec: Open one section and add only level marks, not new words: parent, child, child detail. If the marks feel false, fix the structure before formatting.
